scenes.tekst: Do your printed knees bend too far?
scenes.label: TOO FAR?

scenes.tekst: Here's a rigged character in Blender, with Click Joints Pro open.
scenes.label: START

scenes.tekst: Select the character, then press Figure from rig.
scenes.label: ONE BUTTON

scenes.tekst: It puts a joint at every shoulder, elbow, hip, knee and neck.
scenes.label: WHAT YOU GET

scenes.tekst: The panel lists all nine joints, each with its range in degrees.
scenes.label: THE LIST

scenes.tekst: The left knee is a hinge, from zero to one hundred and twenty degrees.
scenes.label: LEFT KNEE

scenes.tekst: That limit comes from our rig. The right knee mirrors it.
scenes.label: WHERE FROM
scenes.kop: The limit comes from the rig

scenes.tekst: Now drag the Bend slider, and watch the knee.
scenes.label: TRY IT

scenes.tekst: At one hundred and twenty degrees, it reaches the end stop.
scenes.label: AT THE TOP

scenes.tekst: Go further, and a red arc shows how far past the limit you are.
scenes.label: TOO FAR

scenes.tekst: So you find the problem in Blender, before you print.
scenes.label: WHY IT MATTERS

scenes.tekst: Exploded view pulls the parts apart, so you can see the ball joints.
scenes.label: EXPLODED VIEW

scenes.tekst: Then export every part as a 3MF file for your slicer.
scenes.uitspraak: Then export every part as a three M F file, for your slicer.
scenes.label: EXPORT

scenes.tekst: Measured in Blender, not print tested by us yet. Print a test joint first.
scenes.label: GOOD TO KNOW

scenes.tekst: Click Joints Pro. Elbows and knees stop where your rig stops.
